To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the 12-ECG leads do not provide the information needed to distinguish acute NQMI from acute QMI and that (2) the combination of body surface potential mapping and multivariate statistical analysis can provide the necessary information.

the combination of multivariate statistical analysis and body surface potential maps provides a powerful approach for the analysis of the electrocardiogram and that it allows the recognition of acute non-Q wave infarctions with high sensitivity and specificity.
the diagnosis of acute NQWI can be improved substantially and that acute NQWI and acute QMI (also with LVH) are not different entities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a practical method to identify NQMI by BSPM.
the development of a practical, computer-assisted diagnostic system that can be applied at bedside to identify acute NQMI.
the application of statistical procedures for the analysis of body surface potential (BSP) maps.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ECG is a powerful tool in diagnosing acute MI, but the information content is limited and can be enhanced by the use of multivariate statistical methods and body surface mapping.
the present study does not support the existence of NQMI as an ECG entity but that it does support the existence of acute NQ MI as a pathophysiological entity.
BSPM discriminant analysis is an effective tool to improve the diagnosis of acute NQ wave and Q wave MI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of multivariate statistical techniques and body surface potential maps provides an effective approach to the identification of acute Q and non-Q wave myocardium infarction.
the use of discriminant analysis and discriminant maps in the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarct is very useful.
the use of discriminant analysis of BSPM allows the identification of a practical subset of ECG leads that provides a substantial improvement in the diagnosis of acute NQWI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 12-ECG has limited value for the detection of NQMI, but that the 120-BSPM can be very useful.
the ECG can be used to identify patients with NQMI and that the ECG should be used to identify these patients.
BSPM are an important tool for the early diagnosis of acute myocardial infarctions.
